terms.gloss: an account, a telling of what happened
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.80: rem narrāre ita ut vērīsimilis narrātiō sit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From narrō: any account of events; in rhetoric, the statement of the facts of a case.

terms.gloss: a setting out of facts, an account

phrases.latin: dīcere quae audierint ūtile est puerīs ad loquendī facultātem, ideōque et retrō agere expositiōnem et ā mediā in utramque partem discurrere
phrases.english: retelling what they have heard is good for children’s speech; so let them tell the story backwards, and run from the middle to either end

narratio.html: From narrō, which de Vaan (s.v. gnārus) derives from *nārāre, shortened by the littera-rule.

sources: Lewis & Short: narratio · Lewis & Short: expositio
Quintilian from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-quintilianus).
